newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Q1 1997 imports rise 27.65 pct over 1996.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Q1 1997 imports rise 27.65 pct over 1996.

text.p: Brazilian imports of $13.707 billion in the first quarter of 1997 represented an increase of 27.65 percent over the same year-ago period while exports of $10.657 billion were only 3.61 percent higher, officials said.
Mauricio Cortes, foreign trade secretary at the Ministry of Industry and Commerce, said exports were boosted mainly by coffee and soybean sales.
Coffee exports in the first quarter of 1997 were $621 million, an increase of 150.4 percent over the first three months of last year.
Soybean sales were 11.61 percent higher at $500 million.
On the imports side, all categories of goods showed increases.
In a statement, the Ministry of Industry and Commerce said capital goods imports were $3.418 billion in first quarter 1997, a 41.3 percent rise year-on-year.
Imports of primary and intermediate goods rose 16.5 percent to $6.277 billion while consumer goods imports rose 38.4 percent to $2.535 billion.
Fuel and lubricant imports, identified by government officials as the trade balance bogeyman in the second half od 1996, were up 34 percent at $1.477 billion.
The ministry and officials said that most capital goods imports were being used to increase Brazilian productivity.

"In the absence of an increase in domestic supply, the rise in investment has no where to go except into exports," said Jose Roberto Mendonca de Barros, economic policy secretary at the Finance Ministry.
